shortlist.title: 국채 가격 잡음(Hu-Pan-Wang) 급등 뒤 절반 해소 → v1 1x/현금을 3x로 (ADD) / Treasury-noise relief re-arms 3x
shortlist.mechanism: Hu, Pan and Wang (2013 JF) measure arbitrage-capital scarcity as the RMS deviation of Treasury note and bond yields from a smooth fitted curve ('noise'). It spikes when relative-value desks lose funding (1987, 1990, 1994, 1998, 2001, 2007-08). After noise has doubled against its own 1-year median and then given back half of the spike, arbitrage capital is returning and forced selling is over. Expected returns to bearing risk are high right after liquidity crises (Nagel 2012; Brunnermeier-Pedersen 2009, spiral unwinding). v1 waits in 1x/cash until NDX retakes SMA200+2%, so it re-enters V-shaped recoveries late. This input uses neither NDX price nor the alarms and acts only inside v1's non-3x states: it can bring 3x in earlier, and it never cuts v1's 3x or its alarm exits.
shortlist.data_plan: (1) HPW Noise_bp daily: https://en.saif.sjtu.edu.cn/junpan/Noise_Measure_2025.xlsx (court check 2026-11-05: HTTP 200). Keep rows dated 1987-01-02..2014-12-31 and drop later rows on read; save the raw file plus MANIFEST.json (sha256, URL, fetch time). (2) VIX control: column 'vix' of jp.mkX(R,M,'NDX') on jp.calendar('1984-01-03','2014-12-31'). (3) v1 states from L.v1_B(std.contexts()[basis]) and the brake from L.v1_parts; labels and block grid from gate._frame('NDX', ..., '1986-01-02'). (4) SPX bases: no noise data before 1987, so they use v1 B ('not covered'). The generator's pre-1987 CMT-GSW proxy diagnostic is dropped (not run, not counted in N). lab 사용: 아니오 (the noise series is not in the lab panel).
shortlist.signal_spec: N*_t = Noise_bp dated the previous trading day (a value dated d is usable from close d+1), ffilled for at most 5 trading days, else NaN and the signal is off. peak_t = max of N* over t-62..t, with k_t the date of that max. base_t = median of N* over t-251..t (needs 252 non-NaN values, so first usable about 1988-01-04). spike_t = peak_t >= 2.0 x base_t. relief_t = N*_t <= base_t + 0.5 x (peak_t - base_t) AND (t - k_t) >= 5 trading days. on_t = spike_t AND relief_t. Overlay: B_new_t = 3 if on_t and L.v1_B_t < 3, else L.v1_B_t. The av23s(.85) brake and the 2-day execution delay are unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): N_p = exp(L.path_series(log N*, 'dev250_path')). Every comparison above is scale-invariant, so the cumulative log offset at block joins cancels except in windows that straddle a join. Real bases use N* itself. The constants 63, 252, 2.0, 0.5 and 5 are fixed a priori. N = 1.
shortlist.kill_test: Type B (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of non-overlapping 21-trading-day blocks from 1986-01-02. Label = the 3x NDX product (3r - 2rf - 2.45%/yr) beats the deposit ((rf - 2pp) x 0.846) over t+3..t+23. Universe: blocks where v1's target L.v1_B (real_ndx_86_14) is NOT 3x at block start. base = hit rate of the universe in the window; cond = hit rate of universe blocks with on at block start. PASS B iff cond >= base + 10pp AND cond >= 60% AND >= 8 on-blocks, in BOTH windows: early 1988-01-04..1999-12-31 and unseen 2000-01-03..2014-12-31 (opened once, after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256). Fewer than 8 on-blocks in either window = FAIL, with no relaxing. Binding control, early window, reported first: run the identical rule with VIX in place of N*. If the VIX rule has >= 1 on-block and its cond exceeds the noise cond, CLOSE as T02 vol timing. A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, SPX 55-85 not covered (v1 fallback), N = 1 and the deflation stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Any failure means CLOSE and a registry row.
shortlist.why_selected: Highest honest p x novelty of the 14 ideas. The input is genuinely new: a mispricing measure built from the Treasury CUSIP cross-section, which no closed lane had. It is fast and change-based, so it survives the 250-day path rebuild. It targets v1's documented re-entry lag on its 23% non-3x days instead of cutting v1's 3x edge, and its relief windows (late 1990, Q4 1998, Q4 2001, spring 2009, late 2011) fall mostly in rebounds. Main risks: (1) only about 3 early episodes, so fewer than 8 early on-blocks and an automatic FAIL are likely; (2) the 1988-99 early window is inside the authors' own sample; (3) the binding VIX control. Court p 0.02 (generator 0.03, cut for the block-count risk). It is the one lane for the funding/arbitrage-stress family, chosen over TED (plumbing-1) and ED-CD (plumbing-3).
shortlist.novelty_vs_registry: Not in WX1-M1 section 2 (58 raw signals), BT1 section 1 (F1-F4) or r2_resweep section 1 (R: ff, ff-y10, 2s10s, discount rate, y10 vol; C: Baa-Aaa, Baa-y10, GZ, HKM). E10 used GSW only for term-premium bond gating. X37's dealer capital and duration supply are balance-sheet data that were never tested. A grep of 600+ allowed .md files finds no HPW or noise use. Nearest axes: T02 vol timing (handled by the binding VIX control); T21 intermediary-capital theory on price/rate inputs (HPW needs the full Treasury CUSIP cross-section, which no closed lane had); T13 dip buying (price-based). The idea_check hits (T03 'yield curve', S06 'arbitrage') are keyword artefacts.

shortlist.title: 방향별 체결 시각: v1이 노출을 줄일 때는 다음 날 미국 시가, 늘릴 때는 종가에 체결 (QQQ 시가 사용, 거래 추가 없음) / Direction-dependent fill time
shortlist.mechanism: v1's signal, states and trade count stay unchanged. Only exposure DECREASES change: they fill at the open of t+3 instead of the close of t+2, so the old exposure is held through one more overnight session. Pre-2014 evidence: US index and ETF price drift accrues almost entirely close-to-open, while open-to-close is about zero or negative (Cliff-Cooper-Gulen 2008, SPY 1993-2006; Kelly-Clark 2011, ETFs including QQQ). Berkman-Koch-Tuttle-Zhang (2012 JFQA) show attention-driven buying lifts opening prices, so selling at the open and buying at the close is the favourable side. The rule has zero free parameters and adds no trades. The delay for decreases becomes 2.5 days and is never shorter than the locked 2 days.
shortlist.data_plan: (1) QQQ daily OHLC 1999-03-10..2014-12-31: https://api.twelvedata.com/time_series?symbol=QQQ&interval=1day&start_date=1999-03-10&end_date=2014-12-31&outputsize=5000&apikey=demo (court check 2026-11-05: HTTP 200 with values; split-adjusted, not dividend-adjusted), or the same range from the session's already-authorized free-tier Twelve Data connector (get_time_series). (2) SPY daily OHLC 1993-01-29..1999-12-31, for the pre-gate only, from the Twelve Data connector (the demo key returns 401 for SPY). If the connector counts as a login step, record the pre-gate as 'not covered' and proceed on the theory-fixed rule. (3) NDX daily price return r and rf from jp.mkX(R,M,'NDX'), the same r MS1 uses. (4) Engine: a copy of the MS1 engine in the lane's code/ folder (eng2-style, with research/tax_min/code/eng2.py as the template) carrying the split legs. It must reproduce v1 to 1e-12 with on_t = 0 before any split is used. Never use index (NDX/SPX) opens: before 2003 they are stale or missing. lab 사용: 아니오 (needs intraday legs inside the MS1 engine).
shortlist.signal_spec: No prediction. Split for day t (only where a QQQ open exists, 1999-03-11..2014-12-31): on_t = O_t / C_{t-1} - 1 from raw QQQ prices, with no dividend add-back (the ex-dividend drop lands in the overnight leg, a conservative bias against the rule); id_t = (1 + r_NDX,t) / (1 + on_t) - 1. Product legs: 1x overnight on_t, intraday id_t. 3x overnight 3*on_t, intraday (1 + 3r_t - 2rf_t - 0.0245/252) / (1 + 3*on_t) - 1. Cash overnight 0, intraday the daily deposit rate. Rule: if the executed exposure change due at close e = t+2 is a DECREASE (a v1 step-down 3x->1x or 3x/1x->cash, an av23s brake step-down, or the yearly tax-payment sale), fill it at the OPEN of e+1 instead. The account earns old position x the overnight leg of e+1, pays 0.3% on the traded value at the open, then earns new position x the intraday leg of e+1. Increases, unchanged days and the year-end harvest trades fill exactly as in v1, so the harvest stays inside the tax year. Days without a QQQ open (before 1999-03-11, and every SPX basis) set on_t = 0, which is identical to v1 and is reported 'not covered'. On the path the split travels with its source day. N = 1. Report-only stress (not selectable): an extra +0.1%/side opening-auction cost on postponed fills.
shortlist.kill_test: Type F (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Pre-gate, run before any 2000+ open is looked at: (i) on SPY 1993-02-01..1999-03-10 joined to QQQ 1999-03-11..1999-12-31, the mean daily log overnight return minus the mean daily log intraday return must be > 0 with Newey-West t >= 2 (lag 10); (ii) on real_ndx_86_14 v1 decrease-execution days 1993-02..1999-12 (SPY split as the proxy before 1999-03-11), the sum of |delta exposure| x the overnight leg of e+1 must be > 0. If either fails, CLOSE. Otherwise run measure2 once with the engine copy. F pass needs dev250_path d_vs_s085 > +0.5pp AND real_ndx_86_14 d > 0. Then FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, real SPX 55-85 not covered (v1 fallback), N = 1 and the stress stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Failure means CLOSE and a registry row.
shortlist.why_selected: This is the only genuinely open door in the structural lens. Open prices are a new input: c3_invent I12 was closed only because the pool had no opens. The rule has zero parameters, adds no turnover and survives the path rebuild fully. The honest expected effect is small: path +0.1 to +0.3pp, because QQQ opens cover only about 54% of 1986-2014 days. So the +0.5pp F bar is the likely killer. Court p 0.02 (generator 0.03). It is cheap and informative either way.
shortlist.novelty_vs_registry: X38 shifted whole closes symmetrically (delay 1/3, +-0.3pp) and had no open prices. frame_break P03 tested delay 0 (-1.29pp) and an intraday stop-loss (+0.27pp; closed, and not proposed here). P11 tested limit orders (+0.22pp). S10/smallseed is a standalone Korean close-to-open strategy, and T16 is foreign lead-lag. None used US ETF open prices or a direction-asymmetric fill time for v1's own trades. The idea_check hits (L01 'exposure', T16 'overnight', S02 'per') are keyword artefacts.

shortlist.title: 해외 중앙은행 동시 긴축 → v1 3배 깎기: BoJ·분데스방크/ECB·BoE 중 2곳 이상이 6개월 안에 25bp 이상 인상 (CUT)
shortlist.mechanism: Policy-rate hikes by major non-US central banks tighten global funding and carry positions (yen, DM/euro, sterling) and reduce foreign demand for long-duration growth assets. v1's alarms see only US rates and credit (10y-3m inversion, a 1pp rise in the 10y over 6 months, a Baa-Aaa jump), so it can sit at 3x through a synchronized foreign tightening it cannot see. Pre-2014 support: Jensen-Mercer-Johnson (1996 JFE) and Conover-Jensen-Johnson (1999 JBF) find lower stock returns in restrictive monetary environments across countries, and Ang-Bekaert (2007 RFS) find the short rate is the most robust predictor in the US, UK and Germany. The overlay moves v1 from 3x to 1x only while the count is >= 2 and leaves every other state alone.
shortlist.data_plan: FRED CSVs (court check 2026-11-05: all HTTP 200), cut at 2014-12-31 on read. INTDSRJPM193N: Japan discount rate (IMF IFS, monthly), used through 1985-06. IRSTCI01JPM156N: Japan call rate (OECD MEI, monthly), used from 1985-07. INTDSRDEM193N: Bundesbank discount rate (monthly), through 1998-12. ECBMRRFR: ECB MRO (daily), from 1999-01-01. INTDSRGBM193N: UK Bank Rate (monthly), 1959-01..2013-03, then 0.50 carried to 2014-12-31 (unchanged since 2009-03-05). URL pattern: https://fred.stlouisfed.org/graph/fredgraph.csv?id=<ID>. v1 states: L.v1_B on real_spx_55_85 and real_ndx_86_14. Labels: gate._frame for both eras. lab 사용: 아니오 (foreign policy rates are not in the lab panel).
shortlist.signal_spec: For each c in {JP, DE/EZ, UK}, build a change index X_c = the cumulative sum of the source's own period-to-period changes. The change at each splice (JP 1985-07, discount to call rate; DE to EZ 1999-01) is set to 0, so no level jump between sources enters. Availability: a monthly value for month m is usable from the first trading day of m+1; an ECB daily value from the trading day after its date; ffill onto trading days. up_c(t) = 1 if X_c(t) - X_c(t - 126 trading days) >= +0.25 percentage points. ON(t) = sum over c of up_c(t) >= 2. All three series exist from 1959-07, so the first signal is in 1960-01. Overlay: B_new = 1 where L.v1_B = 3 and ON, else L.v1_B; the av23s(.85) brake is unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): L.path_series of each X_c. The rule uses only 126-day differences, so join offsets cancel except in windows that straddle a join. N = 1, with no search over the threshold, window, country set or a '>= 1' variant. The inventor-1 BIS nine-bank 'Fed not rising' variant is merged here and not run.
shortlist.kill_test: Type A (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of non-overlapping 21-trading-day blocks (NDX from 1986-01-02, SPX from 1955-01-03). Label = the 3x product beats the deposit over t+3..t+23. Universe: blocks where v1's target is 3x at block start. Early window: SPX 1960-01-04..1985-12-31 (real_spx_55_85 v1 B) plus NDX 1986-01-02..1999-12-31 (real_ndx_86_14), pooled with an era-matched base: drop = sum over eras of n_on,era x (base_era - hit_on,era), divided by the sum of n_on,era. NDX-only is reported but does not gate. Unseen window: NDX 2000-01-03..2014-12-31, opened once after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256. PASS A iff drop >= 10pp AND >= 8 on-blocks in BOTH windows. A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, real SPX 55-85 not worse than v1 by > 1pp (covered from 1960; 1955-59 uses v1 B), N = 1 and the deflation stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Discount an unseen pass, because the generator knew the 2000 and 2005-07 foreign tightening history. Failure means CLOSE and a registry row.
shortlist.why_selected: Non-US monetary policy is information that v1's US-only alarms structurally cannot see, and no closed lane used it. The data are administrative (never revised, exact dates) and have the longest early window of any survivor (SPX 1960-85 plus NDX 86-99, enough on-blocks). The rule uses only a 6-month change, so it is path-safe, and it needs only FRED. Chosen over inventor-1 (same family) for the longer early window, verified FRED data and an adequate unseen block count (inventor-1 itself expected fewer than 8 unseen on-blocks). Known hostile early episodes: 1988-89, late 1997 and Nov-Dec 1999, when the signal is on while NDX rose. Court p 0.015 (generator 0.02).
shortlist.novelty_vs_registry: WX1-M1 section 2 has US fedfunds only. The r2_resweep R family is US-only (ff, discount rate, yields), and its F family is foreign equity indices, EM ETFs, KRW and gold: prices, not policy. BT1 has no rates. T16 (foreign markets) was closed for prices and reopens on 'new non-price linkage data', which administrative policy decisions are. E04/X34 (carry, FX structure) use FX, not policy, and T03/T20 are US alarms and FOMC days. A grep of 600+ allowed .md files finds no BoJ/Bundesbank/ECB/BoE policy-rate input. The idea_check hits (X37 at score 2.0 with no shared words, T20 on '중앙은행', T15 on 'breadth') are keyword artefacts.

shortlist.title: 단칸 대기업 예측 오차 → v1 3배 깎기: 실제 DI − 직전 조사의 예측 DI (제조업 전체 + 전기기계), 하위 1/3이면 3x → 1x (CUT)
shortlist.mechanism: Each quarterly Tankan reports, from the same 200+ large Japanese manufacturers, the business-conditions DI for the current quarter and the DI they forecast for the next one. Surprise_q = Actual DI(q) - Forecast DI(q), with the forecast published one survey earlier, is an unrevised aggregate expectation error that needs no paid consensus. A strongly negative value means demand fell faster than these firms expected three months before. That is an unanticipated global manufacturing or electronics shock, reported by firms that make and buy in the tech-hardware cycle. Hypothesis: US tech prices do not fully absorb this foreign non-price information within the 2-day delay, so v1 at 3x does worse over the next 1-3 months. The overlay moves v1 from 3x to 1x while the latest surprise is in its bottom tercile and leaves everything else unchanged.
shortlist.data_plan: BoJ Time-Series Data Search API (court check 2026-11-05: HTTP 200): https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/api/v1/getDataCode?format=csv&lang=en&db=CO&startDate=197401&endDate=201404&code=TK99F1000601GCQ01000,TK99F1000601GCQ11000,TK99F1150601GCQ01000,TK99F1150601GCQ11000. These are large-enterprise manufacturing actual/forecast and electrical machinery actual/forecast; endDate must be a quarter code. Metadata, including the Dec 2003 to Mar 2004 break note: https://www.stat-search.boj.or.jp/api/v1/getMetadata?format=csv&lang=en&db=CO (large file, fetch once). Drop any value after the 2014Q4 survey. Never use the FRED copy BSCICP03JPM665S: it is an amplitude-adjusted monthly interpolation, which builds in look-ahead. v1 states: L.v1_B on real_spx_55_85 and real_ndx_86_14. lab 사용: 아니오 (Tankan is not in the lab panel).
shortlist.signal_spec: surprise_q = the mean over two sectors of Actual DI(q) - Forecast DI(q): large manufacturing (TK99F1000601GCQ01000 - TK99F1000601GCQ11000) and large electrical machinery (TK99F1150601GCQ01000 - TK99F1150601GCQ11000). Forecast DI(q) is the forecast series' value for target quarter q, published in the survey of q-1. Usable date U_q = the first trading day of the 2nd month after q's end month (Mar survey -> May, Jun -> Aug, Sep -> Nov, Dec -> Feb). This is conservative (at least 3 weeks after the usual release) and is never tightened after seeing results. The 2004Q1 surprise is NaN (BoJ continuity break), so the signal stays off until the next release. thr_q = the 33.33rd percentile (numpy linear) of all surprises with U < U_q; it needs >= 20 of them, so the signal is active from about 1979-08. ON(t) = 1 if the surprise of the latest release with U_q <= t is <= its thr_q, held until the next release. Overlay: B_new = 1 where L.v1_B = 3 and ON, else L.v1_B; the brake is unchanged. Path (HEADLINE): build a step index S (cumulative surprises, stepping on each U_q) and a 0/1 release flag F. On dev250_path, the latest surprise at day t is the jump of L.path_series(S) on the last path day j <= t with L.gather(F) = 1, compared with L.gather(thr) on that day. A fixed-lag difference of S is not used because releases are 60-66 trading days apart, so a fixed window would sometimes span two releases. N = 1, with no threshold or lag search.
shortlist.kill_test: Type A (brief section 4, thresholds unchanged). Blocks: the gate._frame grid of 21-trading-day blocks (NDX from 1986-01-02, SPX from 1955-01-03). Label = the 3x product beats the deposit over t+3..t+23. Universe: blocks where v1's target is 3x at block start. Early window: SPX 1979-08-01..1985-12-31 (real_spx_55_85 v1 B) plus NDX 1986-01-02..1999-12-31, pooled with an era-matched base: drop = sum over eras of n_on,era x (base_era - hit_on,era), divided by the sum of n_on,era. NDX-only is reported but does not gate. Unseen window: NDX 2000-01-03..2014-12-31, opened once after PRECOMMIT.md + sha256. PASS A iff drop >= 10pp AND >= 8 on-blocks in BOTH windows. A survivor goes to measure2 with B_new. FINAL PASS = HEADLINE_MS1 > 0.1616 AND REAL_NDX > 0.3108, path pw_vs_s085 >= .55, real SPX 55-85 not worse than v1 by > 1pp where covered (1979-08..1985; v1 B before that), N = 1 and the deflation stated, glued reported as an upper bound only. Failure means CLOSE and a registry row.
shortlist.why_selected: This is a separate information family: non-US firms' own expectation errors. The first releases are unrevised and go back to 1974, so an SPX 1979-85 early check is possible. No closed lane had this construct, and it is path-safe (one quarterly change). It is the weakest pick. The generator's own format check found no negative surprise in 1990, so v1's 1990 loss would be missed, and no pre-2014 study shows foreign surveys predicting US returns (Rapach-Strauss-Zhou 2013 find the US leads). It is kept only because its honest p sits at the 0.01 floor and it adds diversity. Run it last.
shortlist.novelty_vs_registry: T22/T23 closed US surveys (Philly Fed current activity and new orders, UMich) as levels and 3-month changes, never as a forecast-error construct and never non-US. T28 used US ALFRED surprises against a naive mean, and T31 used G.17 semis. T16 closed foreign PRICES and reopens on new non-price linkage data, which this is. X37's Korean export first print (untested, blocked on point-in-time) is a different country and series. A grep of 600+ allowed .md files finds no Tankan use. The idea_check hits (X37 at score 2.3 with no shared words; S13 on '실적') are keyword artefacts.

rejected.title: inventor-1 해외 단독 긴축 폭 (BIS 9개 중앙은행, 연준 비인상 조건) CUT
rejected.reason: Merged into OV1-C (same non-US policy-rate family). Not chosen: p 0.01; fewer than 8 unseen on-blocks expected at v1-3x (the generator's own expected point of failure); market-linked pre-reform rates for CA/AU/NZ; and the JP series ends in 2013-04. Its 'Fed not rising' condition is a separate variant and is NOT added to OV1-C: adding it would amount to fitting the early window by hand and would raise N.

coverage_note: I audited 14 ideas from 8 lenses (admin, plumbing, struct, returns, flows, techcycle, global, inventor) and kept 4 lanes, one per information family: Treasury arbitrage-capital stress (OV1-A, type B), fill timing using open prices (OV1-B, type F), non-US monetary policy (OV1-C, type A) and non-US firms' expectation errors (OV1-D, type A). 10 were rejected: 3 merged as same-family duplicates (plumbing-1, plumbing-3, inventor-1), 2 repeat the information of closed axes (admin-1, flows-1), 1 has no window before 2000 (returns-1), and 4 fall below p 0.01 or fail the point-in-time rule (flows-2, techcycle-1/2/3). Method: I read the brief and all 99 registry rows, and checked WX1-M1 section 2, BT1 section 1, r2_resweep section 1, the c3_newinfo E3 scout and c3_invent I12. A grep of 600+ allowed .md files (forbidden folders pruned) found no prior use of HPW noise, open-price fills, foreign policy rates, Tankan, TED/Eurodollar, AWHMAN, WSTS or the semiconductor PPI. I re-ran idea_check on 9 wordings. Every hit was a keyword artefact (UST, yield curve, exposure, rebalancing, 금, 중앙은행; X37 at score 1.7-2.3 with no shared words), so novelty was judged by hand. I re-verified data reachability with HTTP codes only and read no values after 2014: the HPW xlsx, 5 FRED policy-rate series, DED3/DTB3, the BoJ API and BIS WS_CBPOL all return 200. Twelve Data's demo key returns QQQ 1999 values but 401 for SPY, which needs the connector. The court computed no returns and no signals. Honest outlook: the combined chance that at least one lane reaches FINAL is about 6%. Each lane's best case is +0.1 to +1.5pp, nowhere near the 30% wish, and type-A lanes face the VN2 record (0/4). Suggested run order: OV1-A, OV1-B (cheap), OV1-C, OV1-D. p_pass values are the court's honest estimates; the generator values are given in why_selected.
